body: Emotion recognition benchmarks often predict one emotion per text, missing many real-world scenarios where two people arrive at opposing emotions from a single shared event. For example, a child kicks the seat in front of her in excitement while the passenger ahead grows angry. We introduce CHIARO, a 1,000 human-annotated sentence benchmark for contrastive emotion inference grounded in appraisal theory. Each scene describes one causal trigger eliciting a positive emotion in one person and a negative emotion in the other, drawn from a ten-class taxonomy. We benchmark seven frontier LLMs and four off-the-shelf emotion classifiers. The strongest LLM reaches 67.3 macro-F1, well below human agreement, while existing emotion classifiers score near chance. Beyond evaluation, CHIARO also serves as a training signal. When combined with an existing emotion corpus, the resulting downstream classifier improves on CHIARO itself and on six of ten external emotion benchmarks, which positions our dataset as a complementary signal for emotion recognition.
summaryZh: 现有的情感识别基准通常为每段文本预测单一情感，无法应对同一事件导致不同人产生对立情感的真实场景。本文推出了CHIARO，一个基于评价理论的1000句对比情感推理人类标注基准。每个场景描述了一个引发一人积极情绪、另一人消极情绪的共同诱因。评测显示最强LLM的宏F1值仅为67.3，远低于人类水平。将该数据集作为训练信号还能显著提升下游分类器性能。

glossary.explanationZh: 针对同一触发事件，不同主体产生截然相反或对立情感反应的现象。
心理学中关于个体如何对事件进行认知评估从而产生特定情绪的理论。
利用计算模型识别文本或多模态数据中所包含的情感状态的技术。
多分类任务中对各类别F1分数求算术平均的评估指标。
目前技术水平最先进、参数规模和能力最强的商业或开源大语言模型。
